headline: Mexico seizes cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro,’ among FBI’s most wanted
author: Diana Baptista, Samantha Schmidt

paragraphs.text: MEXICO CITY — Mexican forces captured a top drug trafficking leader who was one of the FBI’s 10 most-wanted fugitives, the country’s defense ministry said Saturday, in a dramatic raid that set off an outburst of violence in the kingpin’s Sinaloa stronghold.

Elite Mexican military forces were attacked by firearms and explosives Friday as they entered a building to arrest Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a top cartel leader in northern Sinaloa known as “El Chapo Isidro,” the defense ministry said. Two other top cartel leaders, the second-in-command and financial operator of the criminal group, were also arrested in the operation in Guasave, Sinaloa.

The capture delivers a victory for the government of Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum as it faces increased pressure from the Trump administration to show results in its efforts to dismantle drug trafficking organizations.

“These arrests are an important step toward bringing peace to Sinaloa,” said Omar García Harfuch, the country’s top security official. He said security agencies remain “deployed in the state to protect the population.”

The operation was carried out in coordination with U.S. intelligence officials, Mexico’s defense ministry said. Meza Flores faces an arrest warrant in Mexico on organized crime and drug-related offenses and an extradition warrant to the United States for criminal conspiracy to distribute drugs on U.S. soil.
The Mexican military identified Meza Flores as the leader of the criminal group Beltrán Leyva and an ally of the Pacific cartel.

In 2012, Meza Flores was indicted in the District of Columbia for the possession and distribution of drugs, along with other crimes. Since 2017, the U.S. State Department issued a reward for $5 million for any information leading to the capture or conviction of the drug kingpin.

In 2025, Meza Flores was added to the FBI’s list of 10 most-wanted fugitives due to his role as the alleged leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Organization. The FBI wanted him over the alleged possession, distribution and importation of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the U.S.

According to U.S. authorities, the criminal group has operated over 20 years out of Guasave, where it has used planes, maritime vessels and tractor-trailers to transport drugs in the U.S. The group is also allegedly responsible for the deaths of Mexican law enforcement officials, and of other crimes such as kidnapping, torture and extortion.

Meza Flores’s group was identified in 2013 by the U.S. Treasury Department as one of the main rivals of the Sinaloa cartel, whose turf war drove a rise in violent crimes in Sinaloa, including murder, kidnapping and arson.
Meza Flores has a long criminal career in the most violent Mexican cartels. He was considered the “right hand man” of drug kingpin Alfredo Beltran Leyva.
The criminal group disbanded after Beltrán Leyva’s arrest in 2008 and Arturo Beltrán Leyva’s death at the hands of the Mexican military in 2009, and Meza Flores started his own organization.

Since the 2024 arrest of Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada, who co-founded the Sinaloa cartel with Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, Sinaloa has seen an all-time rise in violent crime. The arrests ignited a battle for the control of the cartel, in which opposing groups regularly block streets, burn cars and trade shots in the streets.
